title: Quantized stress-curve: batching x long-context throughput/latency & accuracy sweep
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Produce an experimental matrix and reproducible artifacts that quantify latency/throughput trade-offs and accuracy impact for FP8 and INT8 serving profiles across realistic batching regimes and long-context workloads. We will measure tail-latency (p95/p99), throughput (tokens/sec), and accuracy regressions (perplexity and task-specific metrics) with KV-cache warmup behavior to inform runtime routing defaults and quantization profile recommendations.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end benchmark harness that runs FP32/FP8/INT8 variants across batch sizes [1,2,4,8,16,32,64] and context lengths [2k,8k,32k,64k] producing latency (p50/p95/p99) and throughput heatmaps.
2) Calibration workflows documented (calib dataset, per-channel vs per-tensor, ablation) and artifacts stored.
3) Accuracy report: relative change in perplexity and two downstream evals (long-form QA exact-match, summarization ROUGE-L) with thresholds: <1.0% PPL delta for FP8, <2.5% for INT8 in production candidate.
4) Clear recommendation table (profile vs workload) and runtime routing knob proposal.
description_details:
Motivation: previous quantization runs focused on short-context or microbenchmarks. Customers run mixed workloads with long context windows and bursty batching; interactions between batching, KV cache warmup, and reduced numeric precision yield non-linear effects on tail latency and accuracy. This ticket produces the evidence we need to set safe defaults and a rollout plan for fp8/int8 profiles.
Scope: build harness (perf runner + eval suite), run on two hardware targets (A100-80GB, H100-80GB), compare: FP32 baseline, fp8-e4m3 and fp8-e5m2 candidates, int8 per-channel symmetric and asymmetric variants. Include both post-training/static calibration and small fine-tune-aware calibration where applicable.
Bench harness specifics: workload generator uses a mix of prompt lengths and arrival patterns (steady vs microburst). Use continuous-batching mode + fixed batchers to isolate effects. Measure KV cache hit-rate, cold-start tail latency, and steady-state metrics. Save full traces to S3 + link to console dashboards for per-route breakdowns.

observations_summary: Preliminary findings: FP8-e5m2 hits the sweet spot for long-context latency/accuracy in many workloads — ~1.5–1.7x throughput improvement vs FP32 with <0.5% PPL delta and modest p99 uplift when batch sizes are moderate. INT8 provides the highest throughput in large-batch steady-state but suffers more on tail latency for huge contexts due to memory-copy patterns and increased KV warmup sensitivity. Microburst workloads amplify tail regressions for INT8 unless adaptive microbatch coalescing is enabled.
decision_proposal: Temporarily mark fp8-e5m2 as the default 'latency-optimized' quant profile for hosted API routes that have context <=32k and latency SLOs. Mark int8-per-channel as 'throughput-optimized' for Dedicated pools with explicit QA gating and autoscale policy. Add runtime flag to enforce 'kv-cache-warmup' grace period when switching profile to avoid cold-start tail spikes. Proposal doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/quant/profile-decision-ENG-200987
